Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

me if you need me to bring the folding music stand from the youth room period", "output": "Hi Dana, I wanted to send you the full plan for the little music fundraiser before we print the handouts. We are raising money for the East Harbor Youth Music Room, and the event is at the Old Ferry Hall on Friday, May 17, from 6:30 to 9:30 in the evening. I first said Saturday, but I mean Friday the 17th. The hall is on Pier Street beside the public library, and the entrance we can use is the blue door facing the bus stop. The library closes at six, so people should not try the main library entrance. Could you check whether the door sign can say “Fundraiser Entrance” and include an arrow, because the blue door is easy to miss after dark?

The idea is a small acoustic evening rather than a formal concert. We have three local performers confirmed: Nia Cole on guitar, the Harbor Strings Duo, and Eli Park on piano. Nia will play two original songs and one folk song; the duo has asked for one music stand and a chair for each player; and Eli needs the upright piano moved away from the wall by about a foot. I am not sure yet whether the piano tuner can come that afternoon, so please leave that detail out of the handout for now. We have four short sets with a break between the second and third, and the last set should finish by nine so we have half an hour to clear the room. Nobody is expected to stay for the cleanup, but we should ask two volunteers to help stack chairs.

The room holds about seventy people seated, but the fire marshal asked us to leave the center aisle clear and keep the back exit unobstructed. We can put thirty-six folding chairs in six rows, with two chairs reserved in the front row for the performers’ guests. The ticket table should sit inside the blue door and not in the hallway, since the building manager says the hallway has to remain clear. We have forty advance tickets at twelve dollars each and twenty at the door for fifteen dollars each. Children under twelve can come in for five dollars, but they still need a ticket so we can count the seats. Please make the sign say “Cash or card accepted,” even though we are still waiting to hear whether the card reader will connect to the hall Wi-Fi. If it does not work, we will take cash and write down the names of anyone who needs a receipt.

For the handout, could you use this wording in the short description: “An evening of local music in support of the East Harbor Youth Music Room. Hear original songs and familiar tunes, meet the musicians during the break, and help us keep free instrument lessons available for local young people.” I like that it sounds welcoming without promising a particular amount of money or a new program. Please do not call it a benefit concert, because Nia says that phrase sounds too formal for this one. We can say “fundraiser” in the title and include the youth music room’s name beneath it. The room has been running its Saturday lessons for six years, and it currently lends instruments to about twenty students, mostly guitars and violins. Those details are useful, but maybe they belong in the welcome remarks rather than on the small handout.

The running order is still flexible, but this is the version I want you to put in the volunteer sheet for now:
1. Doors open at 6:30, and the playlist starts quietly.
2. At 6:50, I welcome people, thank the hall staff, and give a brief explanation of the fundraiser.
3. Nia plays from 7:00 to 7:20, then we take a five-minute reset.
4. The Harbor Strings Duo plays from 7:25 to 7:50.
5. We have a fifteen-minute break with tea and cookies in the side room.
6. Eli plays from 8:05 until 8:30.
7. Nia and Eli have offered to play one song together at 8:35, if the piano is ready.
8. The final group of songs starts at 8:45 and ends by 9:00.

That’s the schedule to print, but please mark the shared song as tentative on the volunteer copy.

For refreshments, we have two large flasks of tea, one small flask of decaf coffee, and bottled water. Jo and Maribel offered to bring cookies, but they have not told me how many yet. Please ask them to label anything that contains nuts, and put the ingredient cards in front of the plates. We should have a separate plate for the gluten-free cookies, not a separate table. The hall kitchen has a kettle and a small refrigerator, but no oven, so we cannot promise to warm food. I can bring paper cups, napkins, and compostable plates from the community center, and I have asked the hall manager whether we can use their recycling bins. She has not answered yet, so don’t list recycling instructions on the sign.

We have a materials budget of two hundred and forty dollars, including the hall rental. The rental is one hundred and twenty dollars, printing is estimated at twenty-eight dollars, refreshments should stay under forty-five dollars, and the rest is for instrument transport and small supplies. Nia has said she can bring her own guitar and stand, and Eli can walk from home with his music folder. The duo needs a ride for two instruments, one cello and one violin, from the north end. I can pick them up if the show ends before 5:30 at the community center, but I cannot carry the cello up the hall steps by myself. Could you ask Sam whether he can meet me there? If he cannot, I will ask the hall manager if the side ramp is available. That is a question only, not a booking yet.

For the volunteers, we have Leah at the ticket table, Marcus greeting people at the door, and you helping with the stage and performer check-in. We still need one person to watch the tea table during the break and one person to count chairs after the audience leaves. If you can ask the high school music club, please tell them the shift is 6:00 to 7:30 or 8:30 to 9:30, not the whole evening. People can take one shift or both, and we can offer them a free ticket for another event at the hall. I do not know the date of that event yet, so just say we can follow up later. Please bring the printed performer list, a roll of painter’s tape, and the black marker from my desk. The microphone is not needed, because everyone will be close enough to the front of the room.

Finally, can you send me the handout draft by Tuesday afternoon and the volunteer sheet by Thursday lunch? I can check names and times that evening, then take the files to the print shop on Friday morning. Use a plain, readable typeface, one page for the handout and one page for the volunteer sheet. The handout should include the library landmark and the blue door, but not the performer phone numbers. I have permission to list the performers’ names, not their personal contact details. If you are unsure about any of the wording, leave me a note instead of guessing.
